chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah said: A sheikh from the descendants of Adi ibn Hatim narrated to me from his father from his grandfather, Adi ibn Hatim, who was with Ali (peace be upon him) in his campaign:

That Ali (peace be upon him) said on the day he met Mu'awiya (may God curse him) at Siffin, and he raised his voice with it so his companions could hear: 'By God, I will surely kill Mu'awiya and his companions.' Then he said at the end of his statement, 'If God wills,' and lowered his voice with it. I was near him, so I said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, you swore on what you said, then you made an exception (istithna'), so what did you intend by that?'

He said: 'Indeed, war is deception, and I am not a liar among the believers. So I intended to encourage my companions against them so that they would not falter and so that they would hope in them. Understand, for you will benefit from it after today, if God wills.'

And know that God, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Moses (peace be upon him) when He sent him to Pharaoh: 'So go to him' and 'Speak to him with a gentle word, perhaps he will be reminded or fear.' And He knew that he would not be reminded nor fear, but so that it would make Moses (peace be upon him) more eager to go.'

key_terms.اِسْتَثْنَى: To make an exception (grammatically adding 'if God wills' to an oath)
key_terms.صِفِّينَ: Siffin (the battlefield where Ali fought Mu'awiya)
key_terms.قَوْلاً لَيِّناً: A gentle word (Quranic phrase from Surah Taha)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'war is deception' in Shia hadith and how did Ali (peace be upon him) apply it at Siffin?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the concept of *khuda'ah* (strategic deception) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing Ali’s tactical encouragement of his troops from mere falsehood. By citing the Quranic narrative of Moses and Pharaoh, the Imam demonstrates that divine wisdom permits using words that are technically true or effective for a specific purpose, even if the literal outcome differs from the immediate expectation, thereby validating the permissibility of tactical ambiguity in warfare.
